findings.description: The `self._pool.release(conn)` call on line 96 sits after the try/except, not in a finally block. The except branch re-raises, so every InventoryError (InsufficientStock, UnknownSku, DuplicateReservation) exits the function before release runs. Each rejected reservation, which is a common business outcome when stock is short, leaks a pooled connection. Under load the pool is exhausted and later callers block or fail. Non-InventoryError exceptions (for example a database error) also skip both rollback and release.
findings.suggestion: Move the release into a finally block, as cancel() and level() already do: wrap the try/except in try/finally and call self._pool.release(conn) in the finally clause, keeping conn.rollback() in the except path.
findings.title: Connection never released when reserve() raises an InventoryError
